summary.intent: Get the caliper repo (a Rust/OXC replacement for react-docgen-typescript) to a proper first release on the latest callisto, then clean up and simplify CI gates, ADRs, docs, trails and dependabot handling.
summary.outcome: Release prep PR #33 was merged, the release PR was fixed (oxfmt ignores generated changelogs) and callisto published 0.2.0. Later work landed OXC 0.155 (#253), Callisto 0.16.0 (#255) and a simplified weekly measurement setup (#256), and removed the dead Homebrew notifier (#258). Trails #87, #88 and #30 were set up, and forks were started for the apps/oracle and docs/ADR/dependabot PRs, which were still running at the end.

repo: Callisto releases any package whose version has no tag; with unreleased 0.1.0 the old release PR would skip to 0.1.1, so a minor changeset was added to make the first release 0.2.0.
npm provenance (NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE) requires package.json repository.url to match the GitHub repo, hence the oxc-react-docgen to caliper URL fix across 13 package.json files.
oxfmt rewrites double-quoted scoped package names in changesets to single quotes, which callisto does not strip; the name must be left unquoted.
Callisto-generated CHANGELOG.md files fail `oxfmt --check`, so release PRs failed Lint until `**/CHANGELOG.md` was added to ignorePatterns in .oxfmtrc.json.
Local main had 8 commits that were never pushed (including tsc-client and ADR 0006), so checking `rev-list --left-right main...origin/main` early would have exposed this.
The Homebrew tap is now pull-based: livecheck matches tags like `npm/caliper-docgen@x.y.z` and builds crates/cli from source, so no notifier step is needed in release.yml.
apps/validate holds the TS 7.1 oracle (kept, used by weekly.py --oracle) plus an obsolete July fixtures harness (about 1,250 lines); tsx for CI config tests comes from that package.

The Equivalence allow-list machinery cost more than it caught, so the PR gates were replaced with a weekly job, scripts/weekly.py, and a local `just bench`. The old criterion recipe is now `just bench-criterion`.
OXC 0.155 made string literals and property names JSStr, which broke Display and as_str; a small js_text module maps lone surrogates to U+FFFD.
Callisto 0.15 removed the [init] and [release.profiles] tables and the setup_git_user input, and now restricts which paths a version commit may touch; none of these affect caliper.
A release PR branch pushed with GITHUB_TOKEN gets no CI checks attached.

code.finding: The --out missing-parent test substring-matched a path that miette word-wraps when the CI temp path is long, making it fail in CI only; the test now unwraps the output.
Held the tag-finder and notify-homebrew-tap steps, which were dead after the tap moved to a pull model; removed in #258.
The header comment pins the callisto version and went stale versus the workflow pins; it must be updated alongside ci.yml and release.yml.

friction: The user's recollection of a callisto blocker could not be confirmed from the repo or docs.
Early statements were wrong because the local main was stale (0.8.0 pins, missing tsc-client); they had to be corrected.
git and gh commands were intermittently hooked or blocked, forcing /usr/bin/git and retried commands.
Stash apply silently did nothing and the carried changes had to be re-applied from a patch.
CI on main was red from transient install-action errors, a newly bumped oxfmt flagging archive docs, and stray allow-list files, each needing its own small PR.
Merging dependabot PRs triggered release-PR refreshes, and the user merged those instead of the release PR, causing confusion about whether anything was published.
The first publish attempt on #22's merge ran version-pr instead of plan/build/execute, so the release-candidate detection was still being investigated when the transcript was cut off.
A fork's first `callisto version` edited release files in the parent worktree and had to be reverted.
The apps/oracle fork failed on its first launch because it could not get a writable worktree and had to be relaunched with isolation.
The earlier #236 Homebrew notifier work was built against an outdated flow.
open_items: Confirm the release actually published; the earlier run was green but registries and tags showed nothing, and why release-candidate skipped plan/execute was not resolved in the visible transcript.
Merge #239 as the first release on Callisto 0.16.0, and check that the pull-based tap picks up the tag and opens a formula PR with bottles.
Finish the apps/validate to apps/oracle PR (trail #87) and the docs/ADR/dependabot PRs (trail #88); both forks were still running.
Close dependabot #247 and #248 and add the oxc_* dependabot group; OXC 0.156 is already out.
Retire ADRs 0013, 0021, 0023 and 0024, and review 0002, 0003, 0008, 0009, 0010, 0011, 0012, 0014 and 0019 against the architecture-only test.
Run the weekly workflow by hand once after #256 to validate the corpus installs, cache, artifact download and issue step.
Protect main: confirm no ruleset bypass, require signed commits, and check merge-queue interaction; remove deleted required checks from Entire Gates if any.

Delete the TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID and TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY secrets, stale remote and local scratch branches, and leftover ~/Projects caliper-homebrew-tap and callisto-homebrew-tap worktrees; close stale trails.
Handle .claude/settings.json and .gemini/settings.json tool-config changes, which remained uncommitted and potentially destructive (removed deny rule, emptied plugins, wiped Gemini hooks).
Accuracy gaps: dropped syntax (readonly, index signatures, RefObject), memo(forwardRef) detection, Chakra NonNullable<union>, and shadcn/antd recall.
An intermittent `just test-rust` failure under parallel load was seen once and never identified.
Later features: TS 7.1 on-demand follow-ups, an in-process API for monokl agents, and Storybook latency tracking.
